title: Operator Competency & Incident Evidence Handbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This handbook prescribes the operator competency levels and the Incident Evidence Package (IEP) lifecycle used by Redwood Inference for on-call and incident response. It standardizes what to collect during and after an incident, how to store and name artifacts, who owns retention decisions, and how operator skills are assessed and renewed. The audience includes bridge operators, incident commanders, SRE managers, compliance, and customer success.

Why this exists:
- Ensure reproducible, auditable evidence for postmortems and customer/regulatory requests.
- Keep bridge operators prepared through a clear competency path and game-day practice.
- Reduce time-to-evidence after incidents and lower risk of incomplete investigations.

Applicability:
- Applies to incidents impacting Redwood-hosted public endpoints and customer-facing Dedicated/Private services when Redwood manages evidence.
- Routine maintenance with no customer-facing impact is out of scope.

Operator competency bands (short):
- Band 0 / Observer: Reads runbooks, shadows bridges. Training: 1 shadow shift.
- Band 1 / Operator: Executes standard bridges, collects IEP items. Training: checklist + supervised run.
- Band 2 / Senior Operator: Runs multi-region bridges, prepares IEP for IC. Training: proctored sim + mentor sign-off.
- Band 3 / Lead: Coaches operators, validates evidence completeness on high-impact incidents. Training: demonstrated leadership in multiple incidents and game-days.
- Band 4 / Incident Commander: Owns tactical decisions and customer escalations. Training: proctor assessment and leadership endorsement.

Badge lifecycle and renewal:
- Badges issued after assessment and logged in the SRE credential registry.
- Renewal cadence: Bands 0-1 yearly; Bands 2-4 every 6 months or after major platform changes.
- Failed assessments require a documented remediation plan and retest window (30 days).

Incident Evidence Package (IEP) minimum contents:
- Incident identifier, start and end timestamps, and bridge id.
- Chronological timeline of status updates and actions.
- Metrics snapshots: p50/p95/p99 and error rates for relevant signals.
- Representative logs: -15m to +30m around incident start (sampling allowed with justification).
- Traces/spans for affected request flows.
- Relevant config/deploy markers: commit id, deploy id, feature-flag state.
- Copies of status page messages and customer comms.
- Evidence manifest: list of artifacts, storage URIs, and checksums.

Immediate collection checklist (run on bridge):
1) Export bridge transcript and note bridge id.
2) Capture a metrics snapshot covering the incident window.
3) Export logs for the time window; filter for errors/timeouts but include context lines.
4) Export traces with higher sampling for the first 30 minutes.
5) Record deploy/config state and capture diffs where applicable.
6) Save drafts of status page and customer messages.
7) Publish evidence manifest to the secure evidence bucket and record checksums.

Example commands (illustrative, edit per service):
- Metrics: ri-cli metrics export --service "$SERVICE" --from "$INC_START" --to "$INC_END" --out /tmp/metrics-$INCIDENT.json
- Logs: ri-cli logs export --service "$SERVICE" --from "$INC_START" --to "$INC_END" --filter "error OR timeout" --out /tmp/logs-$INCIDENT.tgz
- Traces: ri-cli traces export --service "$SERVICE" --window "$INC_START/$INC_END" --out /tmp/traces-$INCIDENT.json
- Bridge transcript: bridgectl export --id $BRIDGE_ID --format text --out /tmp/bridge-$INCIDENT.txt

Storage and naming standards:
- All IEP artifacts must be stored under s3://ri-incident-evidence/<year>/<incident-id>/
- Filenames: <incident-id>__<artifact-type>__<short-desc>__v<1>.<ext>
- Example: 2025-03-10-INC-8421__logs__ingest-api__v1.tgz

Retention (summary):
- IEP metadata and timelines: 7 years.
- Aggregated metrics and summaries: 7 years.
- Raw logs: 1 year unless escalated to legal hold.
- Traces: 90 days full fidelity, 2 years sampled summaries.
- Screenshots and customer comms: 7 years.
- PII or customer data: retention governed by contract and legal guidance.

Governance and access control:
- Evidence Custodian approves retention exceptions and legal holds.
- Access requires an evidence request ticket with justification; presigned URLs expire by default after 72 hours.
- All access is audited; audit records are attached to the evidence manifest.

Legal holds and deletion:
- Deletion of evidence requires approval from the Evidence Custodian and Legal.
- Legal holds suspend deletion and retention timers until Legal clears the hold.

Postmortem responsibilities:
- The postmortem author must link to the IEP artifacts and manifest URIs.
- IEP completeness verification must occur within 72 hours of incident closure; missing artifacts escalate to the SRE manager.

Game-day integration and operator fitness:
- Minimum cadence: quarterly simulations per team; monthly for high-risk services (business-critical or frequently failing systems).
- Each game-day requires operators to: run a bridge, capture a full IEP, draft a status page message, and complete a rubric.
- Passing game-day simulations contribute to badge renewal requirements.

Assessment workflow (proctored sim):
1) Candidate schedules a 60-90 minute proctored simulation.
2) The simulation includes triage, bridge ops, evidence collection, and comms.
3) Proctor scores the candidate against a standardized rubric and records pass/fail and notes.
4) On pass, update badge status; on fail, issue remediation plan and retest window.

Severity guidance for evidence depth:
- Sev1 (complete outage or multi-tenant impact): Full IEP + extended logs + raw traces + deploy diffs + regulatory packet as needed.
- Sev2 (partial outage or degraded SLOs): Full IEP + representative logs + sampled traces.
- Sev3 (localized degradation): Compact IEP (metadata, metrics, minimal logs).

Evidence request process (short):
1) Stakeholder opens evidence-request ticket using the template.
2) Evidence Custodian validates scope within 24 hours.
3) Custodian provides presigned URIs or schedules a secure review session.
4) Access is logged; ticket closed after verification or when legal hold is applied.

KPIs and targets:
- IEP completeness within 72h for Sev1/Sev2: target 98%.
- Internal evidence access SLA: 24 hours.
- Badge renewal on time: 95% of operators.

Appendix: templates and short samples
- Status page short template (public):
  Title: Service Degradation — [service-name]
  Impact: Customers may experience increased latency in [region].
  Started: [ISO timestamp]
  Updates: Every 30 minutes until resolved
  Current: Mitigation underway

- Customer notification (CS/Enterprise):
  Subject: Incident [incident-id] — [service-name] — Impact & Next Steps
  Body: We observed an incident beginning at [time] impacting [scope]. Actions taken: [summary]. Postmortem ETA: [date]. Contact: [CS lead].
